payload.text: (hv, 2026-11-20, by selection in the question dialog in vc's session, put after 06:48Z and answered by 07:09Z on vc's date -u; the questions' and options' wording is vc's, each choice is hv's and vc's recommendation) THREE RULINGS. (1) ST0096: A THREAD'S acceptance.md AND ITS COVER'S WORK-PACKAGE TABLE STOP BEING COMMITTED, like steel_threads.md and todo.md (hv decision 66), so two merge requests that change one thread meet in no shared file (hv decision 70). hv chose "Stop committing them", ic's and cc's position, over a file per record (an M package for ic, a tracked file per criterion and test, and still no computed verdict on the forge) and over keeping them committed (a partial reversal of decision 70). Every clone renders them as today; the forge no longer shows a thread's criteria and tests as a page, nor the cover's package table, and keeps the cover's objective and context, each package's page, the attachments and each record's canon JSON. ic's ST0096 WP-02 adds acceptance.md to the declared set; cc's WP-05 takes the table out of the cover. (2) DOCTOR IS RE-DECLARED AS A WRITE, AND ITS BEHAVIOUR DOES NOT CHANGE, in this release (hv decision 69). hv chose "Re-declare it as a write", cc's recommendation, over "Never write by default" (issue 0717's option 3), which would fail CI's pull-request check on a fresh checkout with no store or skip its store-backed checks. The register says doctor mutates, one way (a missing store is made from canon, an older one migrated, as every verb's open does); doctor --read-only stays the door that writes nothing; ic shapes the MCP exposure's recoverability note. (3) vc records hv's rulings on hv's board, as the team brief says: hv chose "Yes, record them on hv's board" after the auto-mode permission check refused vc's first such write between 06:37Z and 06:39Z on vc's date -u.
